title: Nvidia's Financing Web Is Tested as Neocloud Borrowers Feel Huang's Exit
dek: Nvidia's bond yields are up this week and tech credit spreads have widened as investors weigh Jensen Huang's exit; CNBC and Fortune say neoclouds lean on Nvidia's backstops to borrow.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Aerial view of Nvidia's campus buildings

keyPoints: CNBC reported Nvidia's 4.5% bond due 2031 yielded 5.77% on Friday, nearly 6% higher week to date; CoreWeave's 9.75% bond due 2031 yielded 14.75%.
As of its July filing, Nvidia had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to CNBC.
Fortune quoted Switchyard Partners founder Joe Kaiser: if lenders decide the Nvidia guarantee is worth less, neocloud businesses are at risk.
Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider wrote that new multi-party deals at the same scale may be harder to negotiate.
CNBC reported the August memorandums with six financial firms for a $500 billion AI financing drive remain preliminary.
body:
## What CNBC reported Friday

Jensen Huang's departure has not produced a broad shock to the credit market, CNBC reported Friday, but it has put Nvidia's role as a financier of AI infrastructure under scrutiny. Nvidia supplies chips to hyperscalers and tech giants, and it also helps other companies finance their expansion. CNBC wrote that this arrangement "could all change."

Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider wrote in a Thursday note, as CNBC quoted him, that "although we expect the company to fulfill all of its previously announced commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate new multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point."

## Bond yields and credit spreads

CNBC reported that tech bond yields have risen and credit default swap spreads have widened, most notably in lower-rated names. On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.77%, which CNBC described as nearly 6% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

CoreWeave's 9.75% bond due in 2031 yielded 14.75% on Friday, after climbing to 16.7% the week before, CNBC reported. The spread on its five-year credit default swaps fell 18% week to date but remained above 1,000, which CNBC noted is generally considered a sign of distress.

## Where neoclouds are exposed

As of its last quarterly filing in July, Nvidia had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to CNBC. In an October 24 CNBC analysis, those backstops were described as taking many forms, such as guaranteeing a minimum resale price or a minimum hourly offtake price for chips if a lender has to recoup the assets.

CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio, CNBC reported, and their shares fell sharply Thursday. Fortune reported that CoreWeave dropped about 9% that day, giving back part of a 25% rally the day before, and that Nebius fell 16%, though Nebius also issued weak full-year guidance the same day. CNBC's Friday live movers page said AI server maker Dell, chip stock AMD, and neoclouds Nebius and CoreWeave tumbled around 10% in the day's AI selloff.

CreditSights analyst Andy Li told CNBC: "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side." He added that, because Huang was "so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate."

## What lenders are pricing

Fortune's analysis, published Thursday afternoon, argued that the most indebted AI borrowers are the most exposed. Joe Kaiser, founder of Switchyard Partners, told Fortune: "The chip isn't what puts them at risk, but it's the financial backstop that allows CoreWeave or Nebius to go get those hundreds of millions of dollars of debt from Blackstone and Brookfield." He added: "If the capital providers now say that Nvidia guarantee is not worth what it was worth a week ago, that puts those neocloud businesses at risk."

Fortune also reported that in July Nvidia began offering to rent back unused GPU capacity from neocloud partners at a fixed rate, a floor meant to make banks more willing to lend. It said Nvidia later joined a $500 billion financing platform with six institutional partners, under which it may backstop up to $125 billion. Fortune reported CoreWeave carried $35 billion of debt at the end of June.

## The financing partners

CNBC reported on Nov. 12 that in August Nvidia announced memorandums of understanding with Apollo Global Management, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR, aimed at mobilizing more than $500 billion for AI infrastructure. CNBC said those arrangements are preliminary and subject to final agreements. BlackRock and Goldman Sachs declined to comment on Huang's resignation, and the other firms were not immediately available.

Sunaina Sinha Haldea, global head of private capital advisory at Raymond James, told CNBC that a leadership change gives every firm involved a "natural moment to pause and look at the terms again." She said: "I don't think the capital walks away, because these lenders are underwriting Nvidia's chips and the customer contracts behind them, but they could want to be paid more for the uncertainty."

Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo, told CNBC: "This is not a financing crisis yet, but it could become a catalyst for a broader repricing of risk across the AI ecosystem."

## What to watch

Three markers will show whether lenders are repricing. The first is whether the August memorandums become final agreements; CNBC reported they remain preliminary. The second is how Nvidia's leadership questions are addressed at its scheduled Nov. 17 results, covered in our Huang story. The third is whether neocloud bond yields and credit default swap spreads, which CNBC tracked Friday, keep moving.

CNBC reported that "it remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change." Goldman Sachs expects Nvidia to honor previously announced commitments. Until the terms are public, the direction of the financing arrangements is unresolved.

marketImpact.summary: Fortune and CNBC describe Nvidia backstops as a factor lenders weigh when pricing neocloud debt. Any change to those backstops would show up first in neocloud funding costs and bond spreads, not in Nvidia reported results. So far the evidence is wider spreads and yields, not a halt in financing.
marketImpact.timeframe: Next 1-2 sessions, then through the Nov. 17 Nvidia results call

tickers.rationale: The financing role is now under scrutiny; CNBC reported Nvidia has not described any change to its commitments.
CNBC reported its five-year CDS remained above 1,000 despite an 18% weekly drop; lender repricing would hit its funding costs first.
Fell 16% Thursday per Fortune, and is in Nvidia's neocloud portfolio per CNBC; funding depends on backstops lenders are now re-examining.
CNBC lists IREN in Nvidia's neocloud portfolio; no company-specific financing data was reported.
